target: released-checkpoint inference, 2048-sample Landscape/AIST++ evaluation, then published public-data training
required_before_checkpoint_metric_claim: Retain the completed strict architecture-load and one-sample DDPM/DDIM smoke provenance.
Record architecture, sampler, 64x64 metric resolution, random seeds, output count and decode settings.
Map the official 900/100 Landscape train/test split to the loader and evaluator; do not substitute all 1,000 clips without evidence.
Retain pinned I3D and AudioCLIP evaluator weights, their successful self-evaluation smoke, and exact FAD scaling.
Resolve or explicitly patch-and-label the released DPM-Solver dictionary bug before claiming the paper's default-sampler row.
Generate 2048 samples per run and repeat six runs before comparing a main-table claim.
required_before_training: Verify the exact 1000 Landscape clips or 1020 AIST++-crop clips, their preprocessing and source/license provenance.
Freeze 8-rank training environment, global batches 32 and 48, checkpoint cadence and resume behavior.
Pass decode, one-batch forward/backward, checkpoint and resume tests; label them process smoke tests.
Run full 100000-step base then 270000-step SR training on public formal data only.
known_protocol_risks: Paper says FAD is multiplied by 1e4; the earliest public evaluator release uses 1e3 and current code uses 1e4.
Current official code is a 2024 update, not a tagged paper artifact.
README's Drive links lack file manifests, checksums, dataset source URLs and licenses.
The evaluator loop uses the count of batches against eval_num, then slices feature tensors; actual sample count must be measured rather than assumed.
No official paper generation seeds or six-run sample sets are published.
The released shell scripts use landscape/train as both training directory and 2,048-sample metric reference; the 100-video test split is not used by the released metric command.

The current base container lacks an MPI runtime and mpiexec. The official code imports mpi4py before model construction, so a separately pinned MPI environment must pass imports before a smoke can begin.

Both the paper-era and current public DPM-Solver implementations pass a multimodal dictionary into a wrapper branch that reads x.shape, so the released default DPM-Solver sampler fails before producing a sample.
The current release's sampling script imports the full AudioCLIP evaluation stack even without a reference directory; legacy dependency compatibility is therefore part of deployment fidelity.
